TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_CityGuard_0: <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> grew up admiring a father who had served many years as a captain of the city guard, and so chose the same path. At first, the duty seemed noble—maintaining order, keeping the streets safe. Yet as the years passed, the truth became harder to ignore. The role was less about justice and more about serving the powerful, running errands for nobles, and holding one’s tongue before unjust commands. Each compromise pressed heavier upon the heart, until pride gave way to quiet torment.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Poacher_0: As a child abandoned to the streets, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> survived by stealing scraps and catching small animals to stave off hunger. By chance and persistence, the ways of hunters were imitated from afar, and those makeshift methods soon turned into poaching. But it was not long before the truth was exposed, and the hunted life began. Sadly, in the end, there were few places left to hide.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_ExiledWarrior_0: Once celebrated as the tribe’s most promising warrior, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> could not escape the slow weight of time. In the ritual duel that determined the tribe’s First Fang, defeat came swiftly, leaving a wound that would not heal. Tradition showed no mercy: exile awaited those who faltered. Cast out from kin and home, the warrior wandered wherever the wind carried, haunted by honor lost. Yet destiny had not forgotten—before long, the road led once more to a place where valor would be tested anew.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Slave_0: From birth, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> never knew what freedom was, sold to a merchant without even knowing if parents existed, and forced into endless labor. From dawn to night, loads were carried at the master’s command, life bent beneath the whip. Yet deep inside lingered a faint hope of one day escaping the suffering, a hope that sustained a spirit flinching at the mere sound of footsteps.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Slave_1: From childhood, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> was broken into obedience, bound by rope and worked day and night, never daring to dream of escape. Yet every night the torment of flying free like a bird haunted each dream. No matter how harsh life was, there remained belief in soaring one day, and with that resolve to live no longer as a slave, training began little by little toward escape.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Slave_2: <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> endured years of humiliation, and on the day of an attempted escape was caught and beaten until an ankle shattered. Yet even then, the longing for freedom never disappeared. The vow to one day gain strength enough to break the chains with their own hands burned on, and even in the dungeon where tears fell alone, the dream of rising again endured.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Begger_0: The cobblestones of the street were home to <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color>. Orphaned in childhood and left to wander alone, rainy nights meant curling up in the cracks of abandoned buildings, and cold winters meant sleep among heaps of refuse still holding warmth. People passed without a glance, yet even in hunger there was no surrender, clinging to the dream of one day sleeping peacefully in a warm home.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Begger_1: <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> barely survived by begging, wandering the streets in torn clothes and a dirty face, often driven away by children throwing stones. Each time, teeth clenched and tears swallowed. One day, an abandoned church yielded a book found by chance, and in its pages, hope appeared unbidden. That book gave the courage to rise again.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Begger_2: Suffering from hunger and cold, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> struggled each day to survive the streets. Weary with hunger, discarded food from the roadside was eaten while memories of once living humanely flickered, but reality was merciless. A resolve to one day escape this harsh street was born, and that vow only strengthened the will and instinct to survive.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Miner_0: From childhood, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> grew up swinging a pickaxe deep in the mines. Even in choking dust and before walls of stone that seemed ready to collapse, they never stopped working, and with every vein they broke open, their body grew stronger. Yet after spending so many years in the dark, they struggled to settle into the noise and brightness of the surface.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Miner_1: Having lived beneath the earth, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> learned to read the grain of stone and sense the path of ore veins. Even by the faint glow of a lamp, they brought the pickaxe down without hesitation and crossed long tunnels with heavy ore on their back. As the years passed, they became as steady as solid rock, difficult to shake.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Miner_2: To <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color>, the mines were not a place to fear, but a workplace and a home. Amid falling stones and clouds of dirt, they stayed calm and held their ground, and whenever they faced something harder than stone, they found even more strength. But since a pickaxe had always come easier than words, they often seemed rough when faced with complicated feelings.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Messenger_0: Traveling between villages and strongholds, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> always thought of the fastest route first. They never slowed on slopes or muddy roads, and even when they were gasping for breath, they kept every letter close. Yet after so long carrying other people’s words, they were awkward when it came to speaking their own heart.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Messenger_1: After carrying messages across battlefields and through guarded gates, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> knew the lay of every road and shortcut better than anyone. They ran through dark nights and driving rain with orders held tight, and the more urgent the message, the faster their feet moved. As the years passed, acting first came to them far more naturally than waiting.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Messenger_2: <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> knew well that a single letter could change someone’s fate or turn the tide of battle. So they ran every road to the end on tired legs, and even before closing gates, they never slowed their final steps. But after living through one urgent moment after another, they often grew uneasy in places that were calm.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Undertaker_0: At the edge of the village, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> helped with funerals and grew used to wiping the faces of the dead and straightening worn clothes. Even in places filled with tears and resentment, their hands never faltered, and each time the shovel covered the grave with soil, they quietly listened to those left behind. Perhaps because of that, they found it hard to laugh in lively company.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Undertaker_1: <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> often stepped outside at the sound of bells ringing late at night. In cold rooms, they dressed the departed in their final clothes and leveled the soil by the grave before dawn arrived. Years spent close to death left them calm, but they were often slow to respond to the light jokes of the living.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Undertaker_2: Having lived as an undertaker, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> never treated even a nameless person's end carelessly. Before unfamiliar faces, they folded both hands neatly and gently buried lives whose stories no one knew beneath the soil. Yet the more accustomed they became to farewells, the more they tended to take a step back from new bonds.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Deserter_0: After surviving the roar of battle, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> slipped out of camp one night, leaving their weapon and name behind. The shouts and screams from behind stayed in their ears for a long time, and even on quiet roads, they kept looking back. Since that day, they learned to steady their breath before a fight even began.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Deserter_1: <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> never forgot the moment fear moved their body before any order could. On the night they fled across wet earth, the weapon in their hand grew heavier with every step, and even a single footfall made their heart sink. Surviving left a longer shadow than relief ever could.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Deserter_2: Even after taking off the uniform, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> never fully left the battlefield behind. Their shoulders tightened at the sound of a door slamming shut, and when unfamiliar footsteps drew near, they looked for a way out first. Though they knew no one was chasing them, they still could not trust the silence at their back.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Blacksmith_0: Having lived before blazing furnaces, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> could judge the right moment just by the color of heated iron. With every blow of the hammer against the anvil, sparks flew, and dull blades and dented armor passed through their hands to find their purpose again. In return, they grew stubborn enough to believe that anything could be set right if it was hammered long enough.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Blacksmith_1: <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> began each day with the bellows and the sound of hammering. Even in suffocating heat, their hands stayed steady, and they studied the surface of metal for a long time so that even the smallest crack would not escape them. As the years passed, they came to react faster to the sound of metal than to people's words.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Blacksmith_2: As a blacksmith, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> repaired countless broken tools and worn weapons. Folding and drawing out heated iron demanded both strength and patience, and only after striking the same spot dozens of times would the desired shape finally emerge. Yet when faced with things that could not be mended as easily as they wished, they often found themselves at a loss for words.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Carpenter_0: After years of shaping rough timber, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> remembered each day by the splinters and calluses left in their palms. They measured the path of the saw with their eyes first, and with every pass of the plane, they watched which way the grain settled. Because of that, even when looking at people, they often thought first of the shape that would need long carving and careful fitting.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Carpenter_1: <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> could never easily walk past creaking stairs or a crooked doorframe. They snapped chalk lines, checked measurements, and kept hammering until an unsteady structure found its place again. As the years passed, fixing things with their hands became far more familiar than fixing them with words.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Carpenter_2: As a carpenter, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> saw shapes within the grain of wood that had not yet emerged. Even when raising a single pillar, they watched where the weight would travel, and they knew well that one small gap could bring down an old house. But because they were used to measuring and fitting everything, their hands were often slow when faced with sudden change.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Mage_0: After long hours watching candle flames waver and ripples spread across cups of water, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> came to believe that unseen currents moved through the world. They copied spells from old books and tested that belief by holding small embers and cold winds at their fingertips. Yet because they tried to understand everything through reason, they often fell into thought before they found their words.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Mage_1: <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> spent a long time recording the soot and frozen droplets left behind by failed spells. Fire spread when rushed, wind slipped from the hand when forced, and earth did not readily answer those who hurried. The caution learned that way helped them control power, but it also made them overly careful when faced with unfamiliar situations.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Mage_2: Having learned the power of the elements, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> reacted first to changes that made no sound. They read the moment the air shifted in temperature and the faint sign of dry earth cracking, and even a small tremor of magic was enough for them to sense danger. As the years passed, they grew more used to watching the flow around them than reading the faces of people.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Scout_0: Used to walking ahead of others, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> never carelessly stepped on even a single twig beneath their feet. They hid in low grass, watched the wind change direction, and chose the path before those following behind could meet danger. Yet because they had always learned to stay silent first, it took them time to speak their own thoughts.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Scout_1: When <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> stepped onto an unfamiliar path, they first stopped and counted the sounds around them. From places where birdsong had fallen silent and shallow marks left in the soil, they guessed where unseen danger might be hiding. As the years passed, they became someone who looked for an exit first, even in safe places.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Scout_2: As a scout, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> learned to walk without leaving tracks behind. In the dark, they even lowered the sound of their breathing, and when enemy lights appeared, they checked the way back before moving closer. That helped them avoid many dangers, but it also kept them from ever growing fully close to anyone.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Gardener_0: While tending gardens and the edges of the forest, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> pulled weeds and trimmed dry branches every day. When the soil grew hard, they turned it with a shovel, and when water gathered, they opened a path for it, setting things right one place at a time. Because of that, they could never pass by a place left in disarray.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Gardener_1: <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> never forgot what each season required. They spent their days transplanting young shoots, clearing away sick leaves, and cutting back vines that had crept over fences. Because they were used to work whose results only appeared after a long wait, they were not easily shaken by urgent demands.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Gardener_2: As a gardener, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> knew that small acts of care could gather over time and change the shape of a forest. Even when cutting a single branch, they watched the shade that would remain, and when fixing a stream of water, they packed the surrounding soil so it would not collapse. But because they were used to shaping things slowly, they often hesitated before sudden change.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Druid_0: While dwelling in an ancient forest, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> listened to the breath of trees where the wind had fallen still. When they laid a hand on damp soil, withered roots found strength again, and leaves stirring under moonlight showed them the way. But in places surrounded by stone and iron, the voice of the forest grew distant, and they found it hard to steady their heart.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Druid_1: Before calling on nature, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> first waited for its will. They read unseen signs in the moment birds rose all at once and in the brief silence when the wind stopped, borrowing the forest's strength only when it was needed. As the years passed, they came to listen more deeply to the trembling of leaves than to the words of people.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Druid_2: As a druid, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> lived deep in the forest, listening to the sound of the seasons changing. They felt water flowing beneath the roots and the faint presence of new shoots growing through the night, calling that power to their fingertips only when nature allowed it. But after entrusting themself to the rhythm of the forest for so long, they were often late to the quick words and promises of people.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Occultist_0: While searching through old texts and erased records, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> was drawn to names the world refused to speak. On nights when candlelight flickered low, they copied forbidden passages and added their own interpretations beside symbols they could not understand. But after looking into too many secrets, they began searching for meaning even in ordinary silence.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Occultist_1: <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> found torn pages and sealed notes hidden among old shelves. Warnings not to read them only drew them closer, and even on nights when unknown whispers reached their ears, they did not stop their research. As the years passed, they became more familiar with dangerous questions than with safe answers.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Occultist_2: As an occultist, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> knew that every secret came with a price. Each time they studied nameless rites and ancient symbols, their mind wore down little by little, but their steps toward hidden truths did not easily stop. Because of that, they often suspected even kindness of hiding some deeper intent.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_BeastHunter_0: Every hunt left behind broken traps and deeply gouged tracks. <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> studied fur caught in the dirt and the scent of blood, guessing which way the beast had turned. After growing used to long pursuits, they often looked first for places where an ambush might wait, even on peaceful roads.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Carter_0: Each dawn, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> tightened the ropes on the wagon bed and judged the road by the sound of the wheels. They grew used to pushing wheels out of mud, oiling creaking axles, and getting people and supplies where they needed to be on time. After so long on the road, staying in one place for too long made their body feel stiff.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Carter_1: Whenever <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> entered a remote mountain pass, they checked the wagon cover and the horse's reins again. On winding roads and paths near the forest, they first looked for places where bandits might hide, and when night travel could not be avoided, they even tried to quiet the wheels. Because of that habit, footsteps behind them easily caught their attention even on ordinary journeys.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Carter_2: As a carter, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> spent their life on the road between markets, inns, checkpoints, and ferries. When the horse tired, they let it rest, and when a wheel spoke came loose, they fixed it by the roadside, carrying the cargo to its destination one way or another. As the years passed, they came to think first of arrival times and remaining distance before the faces of people.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_NightWatch_0: Only after everyone had gone to sleep did <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color>'s patrol begin. Carrying a dim lantern, they walked through alleys and beneath the walls, checking the gaps under closed doors and the dark rooftops one by one. Because of that, they grew more used to the quiet footsteps of night than to the noise of day.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_NightWatch_1: <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> walked the same route again and again every deep night. They checked cold hearths, listened for arguments behind taverns, and fought off sleep until the dawn bell rang. As the years passed, they began to notice strange silences first, even on quiet streets.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_NightWatch_2: As a night watchman, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> never ignored a shadow moving in the dark. They searched rain filled alleys and the backs of warehouses, trying to catch signs before trouble began rather than after it happened. But after spending so many long nights keeping watch alone, they were often slow to join conversations in brighter places.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_ExiledLord_0: After losing their lands and becoming a wanderer, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> still kept the bearing of their former life beneath a worn cloak. Even in shabby inn rooms, they held their posture, and before strangers, the habit of command still lingered at the end of their words. Yet faced with the fact that no one was obliged to follow them anymore, they often struggled to choose what to say.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_ExiledLord_1: <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> remembered the soldiers and officials who once moved in their name. Now they had to look after even a small bundle of belongings by themself, but even on the road, they first noticed people's bearing and the order of a place. Even as the years passed, the collapse of their responsibilities weighed heavier than their lowered station.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_ExiledLord_2: Even after being exiled, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> did not lower their head easily. Their gestures stayed neat even in worn gloves, and even while hiding empty pockets, an old authority remained in their speech. But because they were used to the ways of a lost court, they often fell behind in the bargains and jokes of rough roads.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_NobleAdventurer_0: Leaving behind a comfortable estate, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> took old maps and expensive gear and set out for unknown lands. Even on long roads, they rarely let their collar fall out of place, and before ruins and mountains they had never seen, their eyes shone like a child's. Yet when things failed to go as prepared, they were often caught off guard.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_NobleAdventurer_1: <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> spent more time in distant ports and foreign markets than in banquet halls. They searched through records left by scholars, wrote down the words of local guides, and grew easily excited by blank spaces left on maps. As the years passed, they came to miss unfamiliar landscapes more than familiar comforts.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_NobleAdventurer_2: As a noble adventurer, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> knew well that wealth and name could open the way. Fine horses, sturdy equipment, and carefully written letters of introduction carried them through many doors, but they were little help against harsh weather and broken roads. In those moments, they felt for the first time that their own strength was being tested.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Prodigy_0: Noticeable from a young age, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> could do in a few tries what took others a long time to learn. Praise and expectations always followed close behind, and the adults wondered how far they might go. But after growing used to easy success, they often froze when faced with things that did not go their way.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Prodigy_1: <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> often found the answer before anyone taught them how. They quickly understood complex rules and rarely struggled for long, even with difficult tasks. As the years passed, they learned how to hide mistakes before they learned how to make them.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Prodigy_2: Called a prodigy, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> always stood beneath greater expectations. Small achievements were taken for granted, while a single failure was remembered for a long time. Because of that, even as they moved ahead faster than others, they could not easily shake the fear of falling behind.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_CursedChild_0: They say that on the night <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> was born, the village dogs howled until dawn, and the well water carried the smell of black earth. People whispered for a long time about lamps going out and bowls cracking after the child passed by, and no one reached out a hand first. So they grew more used to the sound of closing doors than to smiling faces.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_CursedChild_1: As a child, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> was followed everywhere by low whispers. Flowers that withered without reason and the sound of scratching at windows each night were always blamed on them, and frightened eyes turned away before words could be spoken. As the years passed, they could no longer easily trust even kindness offered to them.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_CursedChild_2: Strange things that were hard to explain often happened around <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color>, who was called a cursed child. Even on clear days, shadows stretched long, and the wind would often turn cold the moment a stranger asked their name. But the curse that lasted longest was not some eerie power, but the memory of the people who feared them.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_TavernRunner_0: While working in a tavern, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> found an empty seat before a guest even opened the door. Most of their day was spent catching overflowing mugs, warming cold stew, and laughing along with the jokes of drunks. Because of that, even in serious moments, they often tried to ease the mood with a light word first.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_TavernRunner_1: <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> easily remembered regulars' orders and the accents of travelers. They moved quickly through loud songs and clinking cups, and before a quarrel could break out, they turned attention aside with a single joke. As the years passed, they came to feel more at ease in a noisy hall than in a quiet room.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_TavernRunner_2: What will it be today? was almost a greeting for <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color>. They wiped up spilled ale, brushed off the complaints of late guests, and arranged the remaining chairs until dawn, yet their expression rarely slipped. But after spending so long tending to other people's moods, they often noticed their own exhaustion too late.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_ForestKeeper_0: From childhood, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> worked the trees of the forest and grew strong. Even in storms the axe never stopped, and no shadowed thicket blocked the way. But life beyond the forest was strange, and before the unknown there was hesitation.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_ForestKeeper_1: For <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color>, cutting trees and finding paths in the woods was natural. At misty dawn timber fell beneath the axe, and under moonlight the way was known by shadows alone. As the years passed, the forest became life itself.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_ForestKeeper_2: <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> lived by the breath of the forest. The grain of wood and the crack of branches told every change around. Having known only nature, the ways of the world were clumsy, and the unfamiliar was met with a plain, guileless heart.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Hunter_0: From childhood, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> roamed the woods with a bow in hand. Tracks and scents were told apart at a glance, and when prey stirred, arrows flew with swift precision. A keen eye and quick body soon became their way of survival.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Hunter_1: Living in the forest, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> overlooked nothing. A scent on the wind or a bent blade of grass was enough to reveal a beast’s trail. Time spent alone was long, but sharpened the senses of a hunter all the more.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Hunter_2: <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> knew no hesitation in the hunt. A sign before them was pursued at once, whether it meant long hours of waiting or days of tracking. Sharp observation and relentless pursuit made their bow ever more precise.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Porter_0: From an early age, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> built strength carrying loads, hardening the body while climbing mountains with burdens on the shoulders. Earning a living by delivering goods kept life going, yet relentless labor ruled each day. Still, a goal remained: to be freed from the weight one day and live a life of freedom.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Porter_1: While carrying loads, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> spoke with countless travelers: some legendary adventurers, others carrying dangerous secrets. Their stories stirred a longing for new worlds and planted the dream of one day leaving the porter's life behind to set out on an adventure of their own.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Porter_2: Living as a porter, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> built endurance and patience, never stopping despite harsh weather or blocked paths. Each climb with heavy loads over rugged trails felt like surpassing one’s limits. Yet a constant question lingered: what truly awaited at the end of endless labor?
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Peddler_0: Pulling a worn cart from village to village, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> sold trinkets that carried passion despite their low worth. Dealings with people taught many lessons, including incredible trades and bitter betrayals. Even so, the journey never ceased, always seeking new paths.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Peddler_1: As a wandering peddler, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> belonged nowhere, sleeping by the roadside each night and setting off again with the dawn. Stories and scraps of knowledge gathered from others became a personal map, the only true possession.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Peddler_2: Trading with strangers, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> braved danger, selling precious treasures on some days and losing everything to swindlers on others. Even so, pride held firm. They believed they were not merely selling goods, but carrying hope and dreams to others.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Wanderer_0: Unable to settle anywhere, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> once had a family, but after losing them, no place was ever home again. Life on the road carried endless solitude, yet within that silence there was a search for the self.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Wanderer_1: Passing through countless villages, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> formed many connections but never stayed long. Belonging nowhere, always ready to leave, new stories bloomed with each step—yet departure always followed.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Wanderer_2: Living as a wanderer, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> endured countless trials, never halting in storms or beneath the desert sun. On the road came self forging and the hope of finding a true path, though where it would lead no one could know.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Hooligan_0: Growing up among gangs, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> turned to crime early, guarding position with fists and tormenting the weak. Yet at night, staring into the dark sky, there were questions of what was truly desired, and within lay only endless conflict and regret.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Hooligan_1: As a hooligan, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> gained infamy, recognized as unmatched in the lawless streets. Yet deep inside lingered a sorrow unspoken, and though violence ensured survival, it left behind nightmares that gnawed at the soul.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Hooligan_2: Earning notoriety on the streets, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> was seen as second to none in the lawless zone. But within dwelled a sorrow never spoken aloud, and a violent life that granted survival also devoured the soul piece by piece.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Thief_0: In the dark of night, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> moved silently where no gaze could reach, stealing since childhood as the only means of survival. Vanishing like a shadow without a trace, yet the fear of being caught one day was a constant torment.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Thief_1: With countless locks opened, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> crept into homes to steal treasures, scraping by on what was taken. Life was ever unstable, and the desire was not for mere survival but true freedom. Yet the hands were already too deeply stained with sin.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Thief_2: Living as a thief, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> betrayed trust, stealing whatever was needed only for oneself. Yet in the stillness of midnight, doubts about the chosen path crept in. Gold and jewels filled the hands, but within lingered an emptiness that could never be erased.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Butcher_0: Working as a butcher, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> grew used to handling beasts, sweating each day with heavy tools in hand. The smell of blood was part of the workshop, and the harsh labor built a stronger body.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Butcher_1: From childhood, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> followed parents into the slaughterhouse, learning to handle knives and dress meat. The daily motions grew ever more skilled, and others came to value the practiced craft.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Butcher_2: Living as a butcher, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> saw it as duty to bring meat to family table and village market. The work was rough and tiring, and though some looked down on it, somehow the work still felt right.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Conscript_0: Dragged into service as a conscript, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> left a peaceful village and was forced overnight to cut men down. Reluctance yielded to routine, and the life of the field became habit. Thoughts of home surfaced at times, but little could be done about them.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Conscript_1: Conscripted and pushed into war, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> took up arms to survive, and fighting soon felt like another task to finish. Skill improved, but glory stayed distant; concern shifted to the next ration and a place to sleep rather than any grand purpose.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Conscript_2: Forced into conscription, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> endured on the front. Seeing comrades drop one by one offered no time for weakness, so feeling was set aside and survival techniques were learned. Talk of comradeship and cause existed in words, but in practice each day was simply endured.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_SnakeCatcher_0: Bitten by a venomous serpent in youth, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> trained the body to overcome fear. With each passing year the movements grew swifter, until a snake could be caught before it rose to strike. This skill made survival possible in the marsh.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_SnakeCatcher_1: <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> hunted serpents through the marsh, slipping into narrow gaps, tasting the air, and reading a serpent's movements with their fingertips. Their skill brought venom and hides back to the tribe, and hardship soon became part of everyday life.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_SnakeCatcher_2: As a snake catcher, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> sensed serpents with sharpened instinct, pinning the neck in a single motion. Venom served for medicine and weapons, and the life never strayed from the swamp.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Gambler_0: Growing up in gambling dens, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> learned to read people and sense their intentions from the smallest movements. Life was always a gamble between danger and opportunity, and each victory led to greater risks until uncontrollable greed finally swallowed them.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Gambler_1: Unafraid to stake everything, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> lived as though life itself were a gamble, a single wager able to overturn it all. Yet each thrill of victory was shadowed by emptiness. Risk followed risk in search of the decisive move to change everything, but the truth of what was truly desired remained unknown.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Gambler_2: Losing much through gambling made <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> harder. Loved ones were betrayed, friends deceived, and wealth amassed, yet loneliness always lingered at success’s end. New challenges were sought to prove worth, but only emptiness awaited.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Philosopher_0: Dedicating life to solitary study, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> was mocked as an eccentric. Yet countless ancient texts were devoured and contemplation filled day and night. Still, under the world’s cold regard, loneliness deepened until even the very truth once sought began to fade.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Philosopher_1: Pursuing truth in seclusion, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> withdrew into the mountains and into thought. No matter the depth of reflection, the essence remained hidden, and at times all efforts seemed in vain. Yet surrender never came, for the heart ever burned with a yearning for truth.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Philosopher_2: Through endless questions, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> explored the world, questioning what others took for granted and searching for answers. Yet the world failed to understand those ideas, and solitude slowly closed in. They believed they would one day find an answer of their own, even while knowing how difficult the path would be.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Squire_0: Raised as a knight’s squire from childhood, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> spent each day assisting in training and preparing for battle. The body was covered in scars, yet surrender never came. The dream of standing as a knight in an honorable battle remained distant, even as tireless training continued.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Squire_1: As a squire sworn to a liege, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> followed the knight like a shadow and survived countless battles as their shield. Yet deep within, a question began to grow: would they remain a squire forever?
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Squire_2: Following the knight’s path as a squire from youth, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> devoted body and strength to a liege yet remained in the shadows. The dream of being praised in their own name endured, though reality tested without end. Even now, each step still reaches toward that dream.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Mercenary_0: Growing up on battlefields, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> joined a mercenary band after losing parents and learned the ruthless laws of survival. Seen as a warrior who would guard anyone for coin, there remained within a longing for home and family lost. When the fighting ended and solitude returned, there was reflection on what had truly been worth protecting.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Mercenary_1: Drifting from battlefield to battlefield, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> stained the blade with countless foes’ blood and watched comrades fall one by one. Survival always came first as a mercenary, yet sometimes familiar faces returned in dreams. Each time, discipline hardened again and emotions were pressed down.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_Mercenary_2: Ready to fight anyone for coin, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> turned even their name into a tool of survival rather than honor. Yet when wars were over, emptiness remained. There was hope that the sword would no longer serve only survival, but instead reclaim honor once lost.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_SwampKeeper_0: <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> lived in the deep, dark swamp, drawing stubborn vitality from its murky air. Yet the swamp’s twisted essence hindered the grasp of subtle powers. Instead, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> roamed the mire tirelessly, so none dared trespass with ease.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_SwampKeeper_1: From childhood, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> communed with the swamp’s raw vitality, gaining remarkable endurance. Yet its warped essence dulled finer senses, stifling subtle force. People regarded this strange imbalance with awe and fear, while guarding the swamp became <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color>’s solemn duty.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_SwampKeeper_2: Swamp Keeper <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> trained endurance through poison and mire, yet finer strengths waned, blurred and weakened. With unyielding body and persistence, trespassers were pursued without rest, though the warped balance often drew the path deeper into lonely darkness.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_ChiefBodyguard_0: <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> devoted life to guarding the chief’s side. Armed with strength and loyalty, there was readiness to lay down life and countless foes were faced. Yet the true aim was always to earn trust and safeguard the tribe.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_ChiefBodyguard_1: As the chief’s guard, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> endured battle after battle, blocking enemy blades to shield the leader. Scars covered the body as payment, yet retreat never came. Loyalty became a shield the whole tribe could trust.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_ChiefBodyguard_2: Serving as the chief’s guard, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> held unyielding vigil against threats to the tribe. Obedience to every command ensured the leader’s safety, though deep inside lay a yearning to be more than a mere protector.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_ScaleCraftsman_0: <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> is known as a master of delicate scale craftsmanship. The armor and ornaments shaped by those hands were beautiful, powerful, and coveted by many. Their craft raised the tribe's honor, though it demanded lonely patience and focus. To them, craftsmanship was not merely a trade, but life itself.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_ScaleCraftsman_1: Growing up learning scale craftsmanship, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> refined the skills inherited from parents over the years. Countless nights were spent shaping scales into the tribe’s finest armor, though such labor was often taken for granted. At times, doubts arose over the true meaning of the art.
TEXTKEY_BACKGROUNDBIO_ScaleCraftsman_2: As a scale craftsman, <color=#ccbeb8>{0}</color> shaped works of beauty with delicate hands. The creations became powerful armor for warriors and earned respect within the tribe. Yet seeing the art reduced to tools of war, reflection grew on whether the work still followed the right path.
TEXTKEY_GAMEGUIDE_WipNotice_DESC:
Hello! If a critical bug occurs that seriously disrupts gameplay, please <color=#ccbeb8>close the game completely and restart it</color>.
 ##
 TIP: Dungeon Settlers is designed to be a challenging game. <color=#ccbeb8>Clearing it in a single attempt is very difficult.</color> If the situation turns too unfavorable or you are defeated, don’t hesitate to quit and <color=#ccbeb8>start a new campaign to try again multiple times!</color>
##
TIP2: You can always look up information about the game in the Game Guide.

<color=#ccbeb8><Hotkey></color>
- Game Guide <color=#ccbeb8>(F5)</color>
TEXTKEY_GAMEGUIDE_GameObjective_DESC:
<color=#ccbeb8>A catastrophe has struck.</color> The wicked [Shared_Arcteon] is rapidly turning the entire continent into [Shared_BarrenLand].
##
As the expedition leader dispatched by the [Shared_DungeonGuild], you must build an expedition base and destroy [Shared_Arcteon] located in the deepest part of the [Shared_Dungeon].
##
TIP: You can revisit the game controls and all guide content by pressing the <color=#ccbeb8>Help menu at the top right of the screen or the CapsLock key</color>.
TEXTKEY_GAMEGUIDE_Quest_DESC:
You can check your <color=#ccbeb8>current quest objectives</color> in the top right corner of the screen.
##
TIP: In the tutorial, <color=#ccbeb8>some paths may remain blocked until you complete the quest.</color>
If a path is blocked, check your quest and complete it.
TEXTKEY_GAMEGUIDE_CameraMove_DESC: Drag while holding the middle mouse button, or use the <color=#ccbeb8>W/A/S/D</color> keys to <color=#ccbeb8>move the camera</color>.
TEXTKEY_GAMEGUIDE_CameraZoom_DESC:
<color=#ccbeb8>Scroll the mouse wheel up to zoom in and down to zoom out.</color>
Zooming in allows you to see units and surroundings in detail, while zooming out gives a broader view of the area.
TEXTKEY_GAMEGUIDE_ResourcesGathering_DES:
Building your base and preparing for expeditions requires a large amount of resources. You can gather resources from <color=#ccbeb8>gatherable structures</color> found on the map.
##
Click the <color=#ccbeb8>'Gather'</color> button at the bottom right or press the <color=#ccbeb8>Z</color> key to activate <color=#ccbeb8>Gather Mode</color>. While Gather Mode is active, <color=#ccbeb8>left click or drag the targets you want to gather from</color> to assign them.
##
Unless there is a special reason not to, <color=#ccbeb8>expedition members will automatically carry out the orders you give</color>.
##
If you want to cancel assigned orders, click the <color=#ccbeb8>'Cancel'</color> button at the bottom right or press the <color=#ccbeb8>X</color> key to activate <color=#ccbeb8>Cancel Mode</color>.
TEXTKEY_GAMEGUIDE_GameSpeed_DESC:
Control game speed using the <color=#ccbeb8>'Speed Control'</color> buttons at the top left of the screen.

<color=#ccbeb8><Shortcuts></color>
- Pause/Resume <color=#ccbeb8>(Space)</color>
- Normal~Fast <color=#ccbeb8>(F1~F2)</color>
##
TIP: You can <color=#ccbeb8>pause time even during combat to plan</color> your next move or assign actions before resuming.
TEXTKEY_GAMEGUIDE_PickUp_DESC:
You can activate <color=#ccbeb8>Pick Up Mode</color> by clicking the <color=#ccbeb8>'Pick Up'</color> button at the bottom right of the screen or pressing the <color=#ccbeb8>C</color> key.

Picked-up items are added to the unit's <color=#ccbeb8>'Inventory'</color>.
##
TIP: Gathering and picking up items are actions you'll perform repeatedly. <color=#ccbeb8>Remember that you can use 'Drag' to make these actions easier.</color>
TIP2: While Pick Up Mode is active, you can configure Auto Pick Up using the UI at the bottom right.
TEXTKEY_GAMEGUIDE_SelectEntity_DESC:
You can <color=#ccbeb8>select entities by left clicking or dragging</color>.
When an entity is selected, the <color=#ccbeb8>entity summary panel appears at the bottom left</color>, where you can check various effects currently applied to the unit.
##
You can also access <color=#ccbeb8>'Inventory', 'Skills', and 'Status'</color> through the entity summary panel.
##
<color=#ccbeb8><Hotkeys></color>
- Inventory <color=#ccbeb8>(I)</color>
- Skills <color=#ccbeb8>(K)</color>
- Status <color=#ccbeb8>(U)</color>
##
Allied units can be <color=#ccbeb8>quickly selected with hotkeys</color>. <color=#ccbeb8>Holding Shift while selecting adds to the current selection</color>.
##
<color=#ccbeb8><Hotkeys></color>
- Select all units <color=#ccbeb8>(Tab)</color>
- Select individual units <color=#ccbeb8>(1~9)</color>
##
You can use tabs such as <color=#ccbeb8>'Inventory'</color> even while <color=#ccbeb8>multiple units are selected</color>. Use the <color=#ccbeb8>'Tab' key to select all units</color> and compare their information.
##
<color=#ccbeb8>Left clicking empty space clears the current selection.</color>

TIP: While an entity is selected, the <color=#ccbeb8>'Construction Menu'</color> is hidden. Clear the selection first to begin construction.
TEXTKEY_GAMEGUIDE_MultiSelect_DESC:
You can <color=#ccbeb8>click and drag</color> with the left mouse button to select multiple units at once. Or press the <color=#ccbeb8>Tab key</color> to <color=#ccbeb8>select all units</color>.
##
Even in this state, you can use the unit summary panel’s <color=#ccbeb8>'Inventory'</color>, <color=#ccbeb8>'Skills'</color>, and <color=#ccbeb8>'Status'</color> tabs to quickly check relevant information.
##
For certain structures or items, <color=#ccbeb8>double clicking</color> will select all identical objects visible on screen.
TEXTKEY_GAMEGUIDE_InventoryManagement_DE:
You can check the items an entity is carrying in the <color=#ccbeb8>'Inventory'</color> tab of the entity summary panel.

<color=#ccbeb8>Note</color>: Only items held in the inventory of <color=#ccbeb8>allied units or buildings</color> are considered part of your expedition's resources.
##
You can view the total amount of all <color=#ccbeb8>resources</color> owned by the expedition on the <color=#ccbeb8>left side</color> of the screen.
TEXTKEY_GAMEGUIDE_Tooltip_DESC:
<color=#ccbeb8>Tooltips</color> appear when you <color=#ccbeb8>hover the mouse</color> over <color=#ccbeb8>items</color>, <color=#ccbeb8>skills</color>, <color=#ccbeb8>traits</color>, <color=#ccbeb8>stats</color>, and other elements you want to check.
##
When a tooltip is displayed, pressing <color=#ccbeb8>CapsLock (default)</color> will <color=#ccbeb8>'Pin'</color> it. While pinned, you can view additional tooltips for linked elements.
##
For example, [Tuto_TooltipEx1]
TEXTKEY_Tuto_TooltipEx1_DESC:
You can check tooltip information by hovering.
Press the CapsLock button to Hold this tooltip, and then you can view [Tuto_TooltipEx2].
TEXTKEY_Tuto_TooltipEx2_DESC:
Great! Tooltips let you conveniently check various infomation.
Check out various infomation such [Shared_NotImplFeature].
TEXTKEY_GAMEGUIDE_BaseBuildingBasics_DES:
<color=#ccbeb8>When no entity is selected,</color> you can open the <color=#ccbeb8>'Construction Menu'</color> at the bottom left of the screen, left click a building to construct, and then left click on a placement area to build it. Construction consumes resources.
##
You can demolish buildings through the <color=#ccbeb8>'Demolition Mode (V)'</color> at the bottom right of the screen.
When demolishing, a portion of the resources used will be refunded.
TEXTKEY_GAMEGUIDE_Crafting_DESC:
When selecting a crafting structure, open <color=#ccbeb8>'Task Planner'</color> in the entity summary, choose an item and quantity, then press <color=#ccbeb8>'Add Task'</color> to add it to the crafting queue.
##
In the crafting queue, tasks can be repeated a set number of times, until a target quantity is reached, or indefinitely depending on the selected option.
Units prioritize available tasks from the top of the queue.
##
Units only recognize items in their own inventory, storage, or on the ground as valid materials. Items carried by other units cannot be used.
TEXTKEY_GAMEGUIDE_ObjectInteraction_DESC:
<color=#ccbeb8>With a unit selected, right click an interactable object</color> to initiate interaction.
##
Try interacting with various objects like <color=#ccbeb8>portals</color> and <color=#ccbeb8>treasure chests</color>.
TEXTKEY_GAMEGUIDE_DungeonExpeditionBasic:
Select a unit and interact with the <color=#ccbeb8>settlement portal</color> to plan an expedition. Choose the destination, participants, and items.
<color=#ccbeb8>Up to four members can join expedition.</color>
##
Units gain the [Shared_DungeonStayEffect] based on how long they remain in the [Shared_Dungeon]. This effect corrupts their mind and lowers their [STATUS_Mood].
##
Also, <color=#ccbeb8>monsters may respawn or patrol</color> the area over time, so avoid staying in the [Shared_Dungeon] for too long.
##
The settlement contains no resources other than twisted trees. <color=#ccbeb8>To gather resources, you must explore the dungeons.</color>

<color=#ccbeb8>Caution</color>: If this is your first expedition, the <color=#ccbeb8>second floor</color> is extremely difficult. It’s strongly recommended to follow the <color=#ccbeb8>main objectives</color> first.
TEXTKEY_GAMEGUIDE_UnitMove_DESC: <color=#ccbeb8>With a unit selected, right click a location</color> to move the unit.
TEXTKEY_GAMEGUIDE_Attack_DESC:
<color=#ccbeb8>With a unit selected, right click an enemy</color> to perform a <color=#ccbeb8>basic attack</color>.
##
TIP: <color=#ccbeb8>Some ranged attacks consume ammo</color>, such as arrows. <color=#ccbeb8>Be careful not to run out</color>.
TEXTKEY_GAMEGUIDE_UnitBehaviorOptions_DE:
Use <color=#ccbeb8>'Behavior Options'</color> in the entity summary panel to control unit behavior.

There are three Behavior Options : <color=#ccbeb8>'Auto Skill'</color>, <color=#ccbeb8>'Wait for Orders'</color>, and <color=#ccbeb8>'Prioritize Sleep'</color>.
##
<color=#ccbeb8><Hotkeys></color>
- Auto Skill <color=#ccbeb8>(F)</color>: Automatically uses skills on enemies when [STATUS_Energy] is above a certain amount.
- Wait for Orders <color=#ccbeb8>(G)</color>: Holds position during combat and waits for orders. <color=#ccbeb8>Outside combat, waits in place if there is nothing to do</color>.
- Prioritize Sleep <color=#ccbeb8>(H)</color>: Prioritizes sleep when acting.
##
TIP: Use <color=#ccbeb8>'Wait for Orders'</color> when you need to maintain formation during combat.
TEXTKEY_GAMEGUIDE_AutoSkill_DESC:
When the <color=#ccbeb8>'Auto Skill'</color> Behavior Option is enabled, during combat the unit prioritizes skills from left to right in the Skill Quick Slots that meet their usage conditions. 

During combat, a skill is used automatically if conditions such as cooldown and range are met, and <color=#ccbeb8>using the skill with the current [STATUS_Energy] would not cause the unit to become [AFFECTER_Exhausted]</color>. 
##
 You can <color=#ccbeb8>right-click</color> each skill in the Skill Quick Slots to enable or disable its automatic use. 

<color=#ccbeb8>TIP: For some skills that can also hit allies, it is recommended to disable automatic use.</color>
TEXTKEY_GAMEGUIDE_SkillsAbility_DESC:
Manage skills via the <color=#ccbeb8>'Skill'</color> tab in the entity summary panel. <color=#ccbeb8>Units have main and sub skill points</color>, which can be used to <color=#ccbeb8>learn skills</color>.
##
Each <color=#ccbeb8>skill point</color> is earned by [Shared_LevelUp].
##
<color=#ccbeb8>Main skill trees</color> are displayed at the top of the skill window, while <color=#ccbeb8>Sub skill trees</color> are listed below the divider.
##
<color=#ccbeb8>Main skills require the correct type of equipment</color> to be equipped.
##
Learned skills can be added to quick slots by right clicking in the <color=#ccbeb8>'Skill'</color> window or you can just drag the skill icon to quickslot. While the unit is selected, click skills in the <color=#ccbeb8>'Command Panel'</color> or use hotkeys to activate them.
##
<color=#ccbeb8><HotKeys></color>
- Skill 1 <color=#ccbeb8>(Q)</color>
- Skill 2 <color=#ccbeb8>(E)</color>
- Skill 3 <color=#ccbeb8>(R)</color>
- Skill 4 <color=#ccbeb8>(T)</color>
##
TIP : A level 1 unit has <color=#ccbeb8>enough SP to learn one active and one passive skill</color>. Skills are essential, make sure to learn and use them effectively!
TEXTKEY_GAMEGUIDE_EnergyStatus_DESC:
Energy indicates how energized a unit is. 
<color=#ccbeb8>When tired, units fall asleep automatically</color>, and if energy is fully depleted, 
the unit becomes [AFFECTER_SevereExhausted], falling <color=#ccbeb8>unconscious and unresponsive</color>.
##
Energy <color=#ccbeb8>depletes slowly while awake</color> and is <color=#ccbeb8>consumed when using skills</color>.
##
Let the unit sleep, lie in bed, or rest near a campfire to recover energy.
##
TIP: Use the <color=#ccbeb8>'Prioritize Sleep' behavior option</color> to <color=#ccbeb8>help restore energy efficiently</color>.
TEXTKEY_GAMEGUIDE_Inspect_DESC:
After selecting an entity, click <color=#ccbeb8>'Inspect'</color> to view <color=#ccbeb8>detailed information about enemies and other objects</color>.
You can also inspect the <color=#ccbeb8>corpse</color> of a dead target.
##
TIP: <color=#ccbeb8>Understanding enemy stats and traits is critical in battle</color>. Inspect new enemy types actively.
TEXTKEY_GAMEGUIDE_Health_DESC:
Health consists of [STATUS_HealthHead] and [STATUS_HealthBody]. When a unit takes damage, one of these values is reduced.
##
<[STATUS_HealthHead]>
If it falls to 0 or below, the unit <color=#ccbeb8>enters [AFFECTER_Deadly] or dies even if [STATUS_HealthBody] remains</color>.
<[STATUS_HealthBody]>
If it falls to 0 or below, <color=#ccbeb8>remaining damage transfers to [STATUS_HealthHead]</color>.
TEXTKEY_GAMEGUIDE_Hunger_DESC:
This value shows <color=#ccbeb8>how full a unit is</color>. When [STATUS_Hunger] drops below a certain level, the unit will <color=#ccbeb8>automatically seek out and eat food</color>, and <color=#ccbeb8>hunger negatively affects [STATUS_Mood]</color>.
##
When <color=#ccbeb8>[STATUS_Hunger] reaches 0, the unit enters [AFFECTER_SevereHungry] and [AFFECTER_Deadly]</color>, becoming <color=#ccbeb8>unconscious and impossible to control</color>.
At that point, another unit must feed them until <color=#ccbeb8>[STATUS_Hunger] is restored above a certain level for them to recover</color>.
##
If the unit does not regain consciousness before [AFFECTER_Deadly] expires, they will <color=#ccbeb8>die permanently</color>.
##
TIP: <color=#ccbeb8>Bad tasting food can reduce an expedition member's [STATUS_Mood]</color>, so be careful.
TEXTKEY_GAMEGUIDE_DeadlyStatus_DESC:
[AFFECTER_Deadly] is an effect indicating that a <color=#ccbeb8>unit is in imminent danger of death</color>. <color=#ccbeb8>If the unit does not regain consciousness before [AFFECTER_Deadly] expires, it will die permanently</color>.
##
A unit in the [AFFECTER_Deadly] state can be rescued by an allied unit using [ITEM_AidKit]. Alternatively, you can <color=#ccbeb8>carry the unit on another unit's back</color>, bring them back to the settlement, and rescue them through surgery at the [BUILDING_OperatingTable].
##
A rescued unit retains [AFFECTER_DeadlyAfterEffect] for a certain time. If the unit enters [AFFECTER_Deadly] again while under this effect, it will <color=#ccbeb8>die instantly</color>.
TEXTKEY_GAMEGUIDE_InventoryItemInteracti:
<color=#ccbeb8>Right-click an item in the 'Inventory'</color> to open the <color=#ccbeb8>interaction menu</color>.
From this menu, you can <color=#ccbeb8>equip</color> or <color=#ccbeb8>use</color> items.
##
<color=#ccbeb8>Hold Ctrl while dragging an item to another slot</color> to move half of it.
<color=#ccbeb8>Hold Shift while dragging an item to another slot</color> to choose the quantity to move.
##
TIP: <color=#ccbeb8>Use ointment to recover health</color> when a unit's health is low.
TEXTKEY_GAMEGUIDE_ItemWeight_DESC:
All items have weight, and there is a <color=#ccbeb8>limit to the total weight a unit can carry</color>.
##
Exceeding the maximum weight will trigger [AFFECTER_Overloaded] or [AFFECTER_SevereOverloaded], causing <color=#ccbeb8>reduced movement speed and other negative penalties</color>.
TEXTKEY_GAMEGUIDE_DungeonPortal_DESC:
Each floor contains a [Shared_DungeonPortal]. <color=#ccbeb8>You must find the path that leads to it</color>.
##
Through the [Shared_DungeonPortal], you can <color=#ccbeb8>descend to deeper floors</color> or <color=#ccbeb8>return to your settlement.</color>
The deeper the floor, the greater the danger.
##
When interacting with the portal, <color=#ccbeb8>any units outside the portal room will be marked missing and counted as dead</color>.
<color=#ccbeb8>You cannot interact with portals during combat</color>, so please be careful.
##
TIP: <color=#ccbeb8>The game auto saves whenever the map changes</color>.  
If free saving is disabled, a single save slot will be overwritten.  
By default, <color=#ccbeb8>the free save option is turned off when starting a new game, so pay close attention to your save timing</color>.
TEXTKEY_GAMEGUIDE_Storage_DESC:
When returning from the dungeon to the settlement, units will place the items they collected during the expedition on the ground.
<color=#ccbeb8>Storage</color> buildings are used to store specific types of items, and units will <color=#ccbeb8>automatically transport items left on the ground into storage</color>.
##
TIP: There is no function to manually place items carried by a unit into storage.
If you want items to be stored, simply drop them on the ground.
TEXTKEY_GAMEGUIDE_Research_DESC:
Through research, you can develop <color=#ccbeb8>new technologies</color>, unlocking <color=#ccbeb8>new recipes and buildings</color> upon completion.
##
Access the research window by selecting a <color=#ccbeb8>research building</color> and <color=#ccbeb8>clicking 'Research'</color>, or by pressing the <color=#ccbeb8>'Research'</color> button in the top right corner of the screen.  
<color=#ccbeb8>Left click a node</color> to set it as your <color=#ccbeb8>research target</color>.
TEXTKEY_GAMEGUIDE_Recruitment_DESC:
You can recruit new units through <color=#ccbeb8>'Recruit'</color> in the top right corner of the screen.
##
Each unit has <color=#ccbeb8>traits, stats, and skill trees</color>, and the <color=#ccbeb8>recruitment list is refreshed periodically as time passes</color>.
##
Pay close attention to a unit’s [Shared_MajorStat] and [Shared_Talent].
The higher the [Shared_Talent], the more that stat will grow upon [Shared_LevelUp].
##
TIP: It is common for units to die during expeditions or for you to recruit new members. Don't hesitate too much to recruit in the early stages of the game.
TEXTKEY_GAMEGUIDE_LevelUp_DESC:
You can construct a <color=#ccbeb8>Goddess Statue</color> through the construction menu. <color=#ccbeb8>Units with max experience</color> can [Shared_LevelUp] by interacting with the statue.
##
To [Shared_LevelUp], you may choose one of three offerings for [Shared_Consecration].
<color=#ccbeb8>The greater the offering, the greater the bonus to your stat increase.</color>
##
The resulting stats and inscription are not applied immediately. <color=#ccbeb8>You must choose one inscription and press Confirm to finalize the [Shared_LevelUp]</color>.
If you’re not satisfied, you can <color=#ccbeb8>retry</color>.
##
However, previous <color=#ccbeb8>offerings are not returned</color>, and each [Shared_LevelUp] can <color=#ccbeb8>only be done once</color>, so make your decision carefully.
##
TIP: High level units expect better [STATUS_Mood] fulfillment.
If you’re not ready to meet their needs, consider delaying the [Shared_LevelUp].
TEXTKEY_GAMEGUIDE_RoomType_DESC:
Rooms that meet <color=#ccbeb8>certain conditions</color>—such as size, the number and quality of placed structures, and the quality of walls and floors—will be classified as specific room types like [ROOM_NormalPrivateRoom].  
##
The better the room, the higher the required quality of its walls and furnishings.  
As your settlement expands, try creating various rooms such as workshops, dining halls, and temples.  
##
At any time, you can check all available room types in the <color=#ccbeb8>'Room List'</color> section of the Game Guide.  
##
TIP: To qualify as an <color=#ccbeb8>indoor</color> space, the area must be fully enclosed by walls and doors, including corners.  
Additionally, wall quality requirements include corners, while floor quality requirements are determined based on the tiles inside the enclosed walls.
TEXTKEY_GAMEGUIDE_SleepingRoom_DESC:
<color=#ccbeb8>Private Room</color>
Sharing a bedroom with others can make expedition members feel that their personal space is being invaded.
To provide expedition members with the highest-quality sleep, it is best not to place two or more beds in the same room.

[ROOM_PoorPrivateRoom]
[ROOM_MediocrePrivateRoom]
[ROOM_NormalPrivateRoom]
[ROOM_DecentPrivateRoom]

<color=#ccbeb8>Shared Room</color>
When circumstances are tight, expedition members may sometimes have to sleep together in one place.
This may not provide a large mood increase, but it can still be strategically necessary.

[ROOM_PoorSharedRoom]
[ROOM_MediocreSharedRoom]
[ROOM_NormalSharedRoom]
[ROOM_DecentSharedRoom]
TEXTKEY_GAMEGUIDE_Workshop_DESC:
<color=#ccbeb8>Workshop</color>
A space prepared for work. Increases work speed.

[ROOM_PoorWorkshop]
[ROOM_MediocreWorkshop]
[ROOM_NormalWorkshop]
[ROOM_DecentWorkshop]

<color=#ccbeb8>Magic Workshop</color>
A space prepared for magical work. Increases work speed.

[ROOM_PoorMagicWorkshop]
[ROOM_MediocreMagicWorkshop]
[ROOM_NormalMagicWorkshop]
[ROOM_DecentMagicWorkshop]
TEXTKEY_GAMEGUIDE_Lab_DESC:
<color=#ccbeb8>Research Lab</color>
A space prepared for research. Increases research speed.

[ROOM_PoorResearchLab]
[ROOM_MediocreResearchLab]
[ROOM_NormalResearchLab]
[ROOM_DecentResearchLab]
TEXTKEY_GAMEGUIDE_Temple_DESC:
<color=#ccbeb8>Temple</color>
A place for worshipping the Goddess. The more sacred the place becomes, the more willingly the Goddess will bestow her grace upon the faithful.

[ROOM_PoorTemple]
[ROOM_MediocreTemple]
[ROOM_NormalTemple]
[ROOM_DecentTemple]
TEXTKEY_GAMEGUIDE_MerchantRoom_DESC:
<color=#ccbeb8>Merchant Chamber</color>
Once a Merchant Chamber is built, the Guild will dispatch a merchant. You can trade various resources here.

[ROOM_MerchantRoom]
TEXTKEY_GAMEGUIDE_DiningRoom_DESC:
<color=#ccbeb8>Dining Room</color>
Meals are more enjoyable in the Dining Room.

[ROOM_PoorDiningRoom]
[ROOM_MediocreDiningRoom]
[ROOM_NormalDiningRoom]
[ROOM_DecentDiningRoom]
TEXTKEY_GAMEGUIDE_RecreationRoom_DESC:
<color=#ccbeb8>Recreation Room</color>
Allows recreation to be enjoyed more efficiently.

[ROOM_PoorRecreationRoom]
[ROOM_MediocreRecreationRoom]
[ROOM_NormalRecreationRoom]
[ROOM_DecentRecreationRoom]
TEXTKEY_GAMEGUIDE_StressStatus_DESC:
Indicates the level of mental strain a unit is under.
 When [STATUS_Stress] reaches its maximum, the unit enters a [AFFECTER_MentalBreak] state, and [STATUS_Stress] is reset to 0.
 ##
 If [STATUS_Stress] hits the maximum again during [AFFECTER_MentalBreak] state, the unit <color=#ccbeb8>dies instantly</color>.
 ##
 [STATUS_Stress] decreases when [STATUS_Mood] is positive and increases when [STATUS_Mood] is negative, with both changes scaling proportionally to [STATUS_Mood] level.
TEXTKEY_GAMEGUIDE_MoodStatus_DESC:
Represents the current emotional state of a unit.
You can check mood influencing factors via the <color=#ccbeb8>'Mood' section in the 'Status' tab</color>.
##
[STATUS_Mood] <color=#ccbeb8>decreases due to negative conditions</color> like low [STATUS_Hunger] or extended dungeon stays, and <color=#ccbeb8>increases through positive conditions</color> like resting or eating good food.
##
TIP : <color=#ccbeb8>Higher level units expect better treatment</color>, so manage food, equipment, and facilities carefully to avoid discontent.
TEXTKEY_GAMEGUIDE_PauseInCombat_DESC:
<color=#ccbeb8>Even during combat</color>, you can <color=#ccbeb8>freely pause</color> combat by pressing the <color=#ccbeb8>'Space'</color>.
##
While paused, you can <color=#ccbeb8>queue actions</color> such as <color=#ccbeb8>skills</color>, <color=#ccbeb8>movement</color>, or <color=#ccbeb8>item usage</color>.
##
<color=#ccbeb8>Strategic use of pause</color> is essential for achieving <color=#ccbeb8>victory</color>.
##
TIP: When an Acid Bug is <color=#ccbeb8>about to explode, pause the game</color> and issue a move command to dodge the blast.
TEXTKEY_GAMEGUIDE_ConsumptionPolicy_DESC:
You can open the <color=#ccbeb8>Consumption Policy</color> window from the button at the top right of the screen.  
##
Use it to decide which of the <color=#ccbeb8>automatically used consumables</color> to <color=#ccbeb8>allow</color> or <color=#ccbeb8>ban</color> for your units.  
##
For example, you can <color=#ccbeb8>ban</color> units from eating high-quality food so they only consume <color=#ccbeb8>allowed food</color>, or restrict them to specific types of healing items.  
##
TIP: Lizardmen dislike vegetarian food. By <color=#ccbeb8>banning</color> vegetarian meals, you can prevent them from eating it and maintain their <color=#ccbeb8>[STATUS_Mood]</color>.
TEXTKEY_GAMEGUIDE_DungeonCorruption_DESC:
[Shared_DungeonPortal]s created by [Shared_Arcteon] drain energy from their surroundings, slowly turning parts of the continent into [Shared_BarrenLand].
 As the corruption spreads, the [Shared_Dungeon]'s influence grows, and the threats within become more dangerous.
 ##
 Destroying a hidden <color=#ccbeb8>'Dungeon Core'</color> can reduce the corruption level.
 But be careful. The moment you touch a core, the [Shared_Dungeon] will sense the threat and call countless enemies to you.
 ##
 TIP : Dungeon corruption level is currently [Shared_NotImplFeature].
TEXTKEY_GAMEGUIDE_ControlGuide_DESC:
<Basic Controls>

Camera Movement: <color=#ccbeb8>WASD</color>

Select Individual Unit: <color=#ccbeb8>1~9</color>  
Select All Units: <color=#ccbeb8>Tab</color>

Pause/Resume Game: <color=#ccbeb8>Space</color>  
Adjust Game Speed: <color=#ccbeb8>F1~F2</color>
##
Select Object: <color=#ccbeb8>Left Click</color>  
Cancel Selection Mode: <color=#ccbeb8>Right Click</color>  

Gather Mode: <color=#ccbeb8>Z</color>  
Cancel Mode: <color=#ccbeb8>X</color>  
Pickup Mode: <color=#ccbeb8>C</color>  
Demolition Mode: <color=#ccbeb8>V</color>  
##
<Controls While a Unit is Selected>

Move & Basic Attack: <color=#ccbeb8>Right Click</color>  
Interact: <color=#ccbeb8>Right Click</color>  

Status Tab : <color=#ccbeb8>U</color>  
Inventory Tab : <color=#ccbeb8>I</color>  
Skill Tab : <color=#ccbeb8>K</color>  
##
Skill Use1: <color=#ccbeb8>Q</color>  
Skill Use2: <color=#ccbeb8>E</color>  
Skill Use3: <color=#ccbeb8>R</color>  
Skill Use4: <color=#ccbeb8>T</color>
TEXTKEY_GAMEGUIDE_MajorStat_DESC:
Numbers representing a unit's abilities. Each major stat corresponds to the following abilities:

[STATUS_Strength]
This major stat proportionally increases maximum weight, physical attack power, mining proficiency, and logging proficiency.

[STATUS_Constitution]
This major stat proportionally increases maximum health and physical resistance (slashing/blunt/piercing).
##
[STATUS_Will]
This major stat proportionally increases maximum energy, status effect resistance (bleeding/poison/stun/root/disarm), and taming proficiency.

[STATUS_Intelligence]
This major stat proportionally increases magic attack power, magic resistance (fire/water/nature), research proficiency, and medical proficiency.
##
[STATUS_Agility]
This major stat proportionally increases movement speed, evasion chance, and crafting proficiency.

[STATUS_Perception]
This major stat proportionally increases physical critical chance, melee hit chance, ranged hit chance, farming proficiency, and cooking proficiency.
TEXTKEY_GAMEGUIDE_Talent_DESC: Each main attribute is associated with a talent. The higher the talent, the wider the range of potential increase in attributes when leveling up.
TEXTKEY_GAMEGUIDE_Trait_DESC:
Traits represent a unit's background, disposition, physical characteristics, growth history, and other defining elements, and can be checked in the character window. Traits can be gained or lost in various ways, and each trait affects stats, behavior, status, combat performance, and more in different ways depending on its content.


<color=#ccbeb8><Race Trait></color>
Traits that represent the inherent characteristics of a unit's race. They are granted by default according to race and reflect that race's nature or physical differences.


<color=#ccbeb8><Background Trait></color>
Traits that represent a unit's background. Past environment, occupation, and experiences are reflected in these traits and affect the unit's abilities or disposition.


<color=#ccbeb8><Individual Trait></color>
Traits that represent an individual unit's personality, habits, talents, weaknesses, and similar qualities. Even units of the same race or background can have different individuality depending on their individual traits.


<color=#ccbeb8><Inscription Trait></color>
Traits gained by choosing one of the inscriptions randomly offered when leveling up. They determine the unit's growth direction, and the chosen inscription can change combat or daily-life capabilities.


<color=#ccbeb8><Soul Trait></color>
Traits obtained by using soul stones. A unit can have only one soul trait and cannot possess multiple soul traits at the same time.
TEXTKEY_GAMEGUIDE_IndoorStructures_DESC:
Some structures, such as beds or Research Stations, can only be constructed indoors.
To qualify as an <color=#ccbeb8>indoor</color> space, the area must be fully enclosed by walls and doors, <color=#ccbeb8>including corners</color>.
##
Additionally, wall quality requirements <color=#ccbeb8>include room corners</color>, while floor quality requirements are determined based on the floor tiles located inside the walls.
TEXTKEY_GAMEGUIDE_SkillReset_DESC:
If you drink a [ITEM_SkillResetElixir], you can reset your skills.

Skill Reset Elixirs have a chance to be found in treasure chests in the dungeon.
You can also obtain one guaranteed Skill Reset Elixir when your expedition rank reaches [Shared_ExpeditionRank2].
TEXTKEY_GAMEGUIDE_UnitFire_DESC:
You can dismiss a unit by pressing the button below the unit’s portrait in the status window.
Units can only be dismissed while in the settlement.
TEXTKEY_GAMEGUIDE_GoddessTears_DESC:
[ITEM_GoddessTears] can be used to remove Dark Thorn Vines.

The corruption created by the thorn vines will also be removed.
##
Occasionally, a wide clearing may be found beyond the corruption.
TEXTKEY_GAMEGUIDE_TaskPriority_DESC:
You can set the Task Priority for each unit.
A unit’s task efficiency varies depending on its race and stats.
Raising the priority of tasks a unit is good at helps your settlement run more efficiently.
TEXTKEY_GAMEGUIDE_DeadUnitTreatment_DESC:
The body of an expedition member who dies in the settlement will remain where it is. Until the body is properly buried, that expedition member will continue to occupy population.
There are two ways to handle burial.
## 
<Grave Funeral>
If you build an empty grave, another expedition member can bury the body. This is the most common funeral method and one expedition members can accept.
## 
<Corpse Disposal>
While carrying the body, right-click the Settlement Portal to interact with it and dispose of the body. This is considered an insulting act by expedition members.

When the unit’s [STATUS_Energy] reaches 0, they will fall into a deep sleep and become unconscious, unable to be controlled.

[STATUS_Stress] decreases when the unit’s [STATUS_Mood] is above 0.  

TIP: The longer the unit stays in a dungeon, the stronger the negative effects on [STATUS_Mood]. If [STATUS_Mood] is difficult to manage during expedition, it’s better to return to the settlement.
TEXTKEY_ALERT_LowMood_DESC2:

TEXTKEY_RANDOMTIP_6: Units that have reached maximum <color=#ccbeb8>EXP</color> can level up by interacting with the <color=#ccbeb8>Goddess Statue</color>.
TEXTKEY_RANDOMTIP_7: In the <color=#ccbeb8>Consume Policy</color> menu, you can allow or prohibit units from using <color=#ccbeb8>items</color>.
TEXTKEY_RANDOMTIP_8: You can rescue units in the '<color=#ccbeb8>Near Death</color>' state using an <color=#ccbeb8>Aid Kit</color>.
TEXTKEY_RANDOMTIP_9: There are no <color=#ccbeb8>Resources</color> on <color=#ccbeb8>Barren Land</color> except for <color=#ccbeb8>Twisted Tree</color>.
TEXTKEY_RANDOMTIP_10: You can restore a unit's <color=#ccbeb8>Energy</color> by using the <color=#ccbeb8>Prioritize Sleep</color> action option.
TEXTKEY_RANDOMTIP_11: Units in a bad <color=#ccbeb8>Mood</color> gain <color=#ccbeb8>Stress</color>. If <color=#ccbeb8>Stress</color> reaches <color=#ccbeb8>maximum</color>, they enter a <color=#ccbeb8>Mental Collapse</color> state.
TEXTKEY_RANDOMTIP_12: After a <color=#ccbeb8>Mental Collapse</color>, if <color=#ccbeb8>Stress</color> reaches maximum again, the unit dies instantly.
TEXTKEY_RANDOMTIP_13: Higher level units require greater <color=#ccbeb8>Mood</color> satisfaction to stay content.
TEXTKEY_RANDOMTIP_14: If you are unsatisfied with <color=#ccbeb8>Major Stats</color> or <color=#ccbeb8>Inscription</color> granted by praying, you can pray again. Resources are not refunded.
TEXTKEY_RANDOMTIP_16: <color=#ccbeb8>Energy</color> depletion will cause the unit to <color=#ccbeb8>Severely Exhausted</color> temporarily. Units cannot be controlled in this state.
TEXTKEY_RANDOMTIP_17: Deeper dungeons contain richer and rarer <color=#ccbeb8>resources</color>.
TEXTKEY_RANDOMTIP_18: Running low on <color=#ccbeb8>Gold</color>? Treasure chests in dungeons contain <color=#ccbeb8>Gold</color>.
TEXTKEY_RANDOMTIP_20: The higher the <color=#ccbeb8>Talent</color>, the more <color=#ccbeb8>Major Stats</color> increase when leveling up.
TEXTKEY_RANDOMTIP_21: You cannot manually <color=#ccbeb8>save the game</color> while in a dungeon.
TEXTKEY_RANDOMTIP_22: Fulfill different <color=#ccbeb8>room types</color> such as private rooms to gain bonuses. This is especially useful for managing <color=#ccbeb8>mood</color>.
TEXTKEY_RANDOMTIP_23: <color=#ccbeb8>Grilled food</color> greatly boosts <color=#ccbeb8>mood</color> but does not fill the <color=#ccbeb8>stomach</color> much.
TEXTKEY_RANDOMTIP_24: The <color=#ccbeb8>investigation</color> function lets you preview <color=#ccbeb8>monsters' Traits</color> and <color=#ccbeb8>Skills</color> in advance.
TEXTKEY_RANDOMTIP_25: Press the <color=#ccbeb8>Tab key</color> to select all units at once.
TEXTKEY_RANDOMTIP_26: Hold <color=#ccbeb8>Shift</color> and left click other units to add them to the selection.
TEXTKEY_RANDOMTIP_27: Only half of the <color=#ccbeb8>resources</color> used to build walls and doors are returned upon demolition. All other buildable structures return all resources.
TEXTKEY_RANDOMTIP_28: The efficiency of <color=#ccbeb8>Crafting</color>, <color=#ccbeb8>Research</color>, and other tasks depends on a unit's <color=#ccbeb8>Survival Stat</color>.
TEXTKEY_RANDOMTIP_29: The longer a unit stays in a dungeon, the more the dungeon's <color=#ccbeb8>magic</color> gradually lowers its <color=#ccbeb8>Mood</color>.
TEXTKEY_RANDOMTIP_32: Units not positioned inside the <color=#ccbeb8>Portal Room</color> will disappear when using a portal.
TEXTKEY_RANDOMTIP_33: While in <color=#ccbeb8>Gather Mode (Z)</color>, drag with <color=#ccbeb8>left click</color> to assign multiple <color=#ccbeb8>structures</color> for collection at once.
TEXTKEY_RANDOMTIP_34: Use the <color=#ccbeb8>Hold Position</color> action option if you want a unit to stay in place.
TEXTKEY_RANDOMTIP_35: You can check <color=#ccbeb8>Inventory</color>, <color=#ccbeb8>Skill</color>s, and <color=#ccbeb8>Status</color> of multiple selected units at once.
TEXTKEY_RANDOMTIP_36: Drag <color=#ccbeb8>unit portraits</color> at the top of the screen to change their hotkey order.
TEXTKEY_RANDOMTIP_37: In the Inventory, you can drag items to <color=#ccbeb8>nearby units</color> to transfer them conveniently.
TEXTKEY_RANDOMTIP_38: <color=#ccbeb8>Storage Buildings</color> can hold items depending on the types they are designed to store.
